🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICO'S ECONOMY JUST POSTED ITS STRONGEST MONTH SINCE 2021</u>

Despite Trump's tariff threats and the T-MEC noise, Mexico's economy grew 2.2% year-on-year in April and 1.2% over March — the biggest monthly jump since 2021, more than doubling the 1.0% analysts forecast (Inegi). Construction surged 10.4% and farm output rose 4.4%. The 'Mexico is collapsing' narrative keeps colliding with the data.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>A POWERFUL MAN BEAT HIS WIFE ON CAMERA. HIS NEW GOVERNMENT POST WAS GONE WITHIN HOURS.</u>

After María Felicia Jiménez posted video of former Pemex director Víctor Rodríguez Padilla hitting, shoving and pulling her hair in front of their children, his pending appointment to lead the national clean-energy institute (INEEL) was cancelled. The Women's Secretariat: 'any act of violence against a woman must be addressed, investigated and sanctioned.' President Sheinbaum personally pledged support to the victim. No name is too connected.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>MEXICO IS BUILDING WITHOUT BORROWING — AND IT'S ABOUT TO SHOW UP IN THE GDP</u>

From July, Mexico's public-works boom starts registering in the GDP figures, Sheinbaum says — 750 billion pesos channeled into railways alone this term, all without taking on new debt. Neoliberal dogma always insisted you can't build big without borrowing big from the markets. Mexico is laying track, highways and housing and keeping the books clean at the same time.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN'S TAMAULIPAS MACHINE: ~985 MILLION PESOS LOOTED FROM FOOD AID FOR THE POOR</u>

A former welfare secretary under PAN governor Francisco García Cabeza de Vaca was charged this week over the diversion of nearly 985 million pesos — money budgeted for despensas (food baskets) for Tamaulipas's poorest families. She's the second official from that administration to be prosecuted; a court ordered preventive detention but she dodged it with an injunction. This is the neoliberal 'social spending' model the 4T inherited: aid for the poor treated as a private piggy bank.

HOUSTON PUBLIC MEDIA: Trump signals he may pull out of trade agreement with Mexico and Canada, which could impact Texas businesses

June 23, 2026 | 🟢

📰 A US outlet names the actual threat to North American trade — not Mexico, but Trump, who now says "we do better as a country if we don't have an agreement," the same deal he once called "the fairest... we have ever signed."

🇲🇽 Texas has been the top US exporting state for 22 straight years with Mexico as its #1 partner; energy exports south topped $34 billion in 2024.

• Trump: "I would rather not have the agreement... we do better as a country if we don't have an agreement"
• Trade lawyer Michelle Schulz: "It would cause a great deal more disruption than the tariffs have already caused"

AP/NBC: 17 injured when vehicle plows into World Cup revelers in Mexico

June 25, 2026 | 🟡

📰 A driver surrounded by celebrating fans in Cabo San Lucas accelerated into the crowd after Mexico beat Czechia 3-0 — a chaotic street-party incident, with the driver arrested. No cartel, no organized crime.

🔍 The AP wire ran it straight; the slide happens when "World Cup" + "Mexico" headlines stack the episode onto the season's manufactured fear narrative.

• "the vehicle was surrounded by a group of people and... drove through the crowd"
• "Celebrations erupted across Mexico... after Mexico beat Czechia 3-0"

LA TIMES: Ex-U.S. ambassador says Mexico's former president feared Sinaloa boss would expose corrupt officials

June 22, 2026 | 🔴

📰 The LA Times amplifies Ken Salazar's memoir claim that AMLO feared "El Mayo" would "spill the beans" on corrupt officials — sourced entirely to an anonymous businessman Salazar calls "the Whisperer."

💀 Lower in the same piece: Salazar told the paper he "never saw any proof" tying AMLO to the cartels.

• "I never saw any proof of it" — Salazar, on AMLO–cartel ties
• Claim came from "the AMLO whisperer, someone who was a friend and confidant"

NYT: Mexican Officials Have Become Informants for the Trump Administration
June 27, 2026 | 🔴

📰 The NYT headline recasts cross-border law-enforcement cooperation as Mexican officials turning "informants for the Trump administration" — the word frames Mexico's institutions as assets run from Washington, not a sovereign partner.

🇲🇽 Sheinbaum has said for months that US agents do not run operations on Mexican soil; the headline quietly asserts the reverse without showing its work.

🇲🇽📊 INFLATION DOWN TO 3.55% — AND BANXICO NAMES WASHINGTON AS THE DRAG

Mexico's inflation fell to 3.55% in early June, down from 4.45% in April and the lowest since October, and Banxico held its rate at 6.50%. The one risk the central bank flagged for investment through 2026 wasn't domestic policy — it was "uncertainty over the trade relationship with the United States" and the looming T-MEC review. The drag on Mexico's economy has a return address.

🇲🇽🚆 MEXICO IS BUILDING PASSENGER RAIL AGAIN — BY THE STATE, FOR THE PUBLIC

The first AIFA–Pachuca train rolls July 25; the Mexico City–Querétaro and Mexico City–Pachuca lines open in 2027. The price tag: 750 billion pesos, with 33,072 military engineers laying track — 6,380 of them women. The passenger rail that neoliberal privatization killed in the 1990s is back on public tracks.
